title.es: Cambios esperados de DPS con la afinación de la clase del 22 de septiembre

summary.en: Expected DPS Changes with September 22nd Class Tuning...
summary.es: Cambios esperados de DPS con la afinación de la clase del 22 de septiembre...

contentHtml:
With today's weekly reset, many specs are receiving buffs, and our class writers have estimated how much DPS each spec will get!

Our Class Writers have given us a rough approximation of expected throughput changes with the weekly reset based on the class tuning notes and each individual Class Guide for more details. These estimates may vary based on the exact spells that Blizzard buffs tomorrow.

September 22nd Class Tuning Notes

Estimated Class Tuning

We asked our class writers what impact the upcoming changes will have on their spec, and here are their estimates based on sims and theorycrafting! Please click the spoiler tags to see additional information and notes from our class writers.
  • For DPS these are DPS Throughput increases or decreases on both Single Target and AoE.
  • For Healers, these are HPS Throughput numbers.
  • For Tanks, these are DPS Throughput numbers.
Estimated ChangesNotes
SpecSingleAoE
Blood DK0% (SL)
8% (DB)		-2% (SL)
3% (DB)
Spoiler:
Hero talent choice on ST becomes a choice, SL still ahead in aoe
Frost DK4%0%
Spoiler:
Frost is in a pretty nice spot now, but mythic raiders will still mostly feel the pain of the bench until the community perception shifts.
Unholy DK3-4%
15% (bugfix)		1%
7% (bugfix)
Spoiler:
Blizzard is buffing Blightfall which is heavily bugged in terms of extensions and tick time modifiers causing its damage to do way less damage than intended.
Devourer DH1%3.4%
Spoiler:
The breakdown is:
  • ~5.2% ST buff for Annihilator, ~3.4% in AoE
  • ~1% buff for Void-Scarred in ST, ~0.3% in AoE
Annihilator is now the de facto option for M+, although it was mostly adopted at high levels due to its AOE damage. The buffs to ST to Star and Consume/Devour make its ST a lot better, pushing it above VS at all levels.

Doesn't change much in raid, although Annihilator is much more viable in raid if you prefer the playstyle, and might now be the preferred option for Turtles
Havoc DH9%7%
Spoiler:
Aldrachi already simmed well coming into The Venomous Abyss, however, the fight profiles suited better for Fel-Scarred burst profiles and significant AoE. With the buffs, it will likely pull ahead for some fights, including on 2-target encounters, such as Twin Fangs and Lost Explorers. However, it will not always be the go-to choice for all raid encounters or mythic+.
Vengeance DH5%2.5%
Spoiler:
This is for Aldrachi Reaver (AR). AR should perform better in most raid fights and priority damage/funnel situations, but will still be significantly behind in AOE and dungeons overall, at around 30% behind.
Feral Druid1%2%
Spoiler:
These buffs are fairly insignificant, it's a small buff that doesn't really alter the status quo for hero talents in raid, where you should be playing DOTC unless you're getting PI in which case you play WS anyway, or M+, where you can play kind of whatever you want though people will continue to play DOTC.

I can only assume that whoever is in charge of balancing has a cat that's pissing them off this tier (and the last like 7). It's confusing what has happened to Feral's tuning, the spec has consistently wallowed at the bottom of the statistics chart and just as consistently been overlooked for buffs, I don't think at any point has the spec made it past the bottom 3 in the overall statistics. You may say that "clearly Feral is a single target spec, check the Boss damage statistics", and it's clear that Feral Druid doesn't even excel there. We've floated between lower top quartile and the median. If Feral Druid actually excelled in single target while being garbage at other stuff, it might be ok, but instead it's the worst of both worlds. Since these are the last scheduled tuning notes for the season and we've already seen the tuning changes for 12.1.5 (feral not included), any cats out there hoping to have a tune-up should put away their begging bowls, the 5 second rule has passed (or 5 week rule in this case) and we're clearly not being picked up.

If you're an M+ focused feral, then it's a bit of a good news/bad news situation. Good news - congratulations! Most of the complaints above don't focus on you and you're playing the content we're good at! Bad news - the buffs don't really do anything either.
Restoration Druid2%4%
Spoiler:
In raid, about half of the aura buff is compensation for the Photosynthesis fix going into the same hotfix. In Mythic+, you'll get the full 4%.
Augmentation Evoker3%5%
Spoiler:
It's unclear if Duplicate damage will also be buffed, which would be an additional 1% gain to both. These changes are small buffs to personal damage in a season where Augmentation is back to focusing on buff damage and gearing heavily into Mastery. That said, these buffs are welcome, and should especially help Augmentation players in less-coordinated Raid groups, and as well as in Mythic+.
Devastation Evoker1%4%
Spoiler:
Flameshaper gets a bigger gain specifically in single target and is now ahead of Scalecommander by 4% on strictly Single Target. If you consider swapping to Flameshaper for ST, it would be 4% AoE and 5% ST. I don't think that's reasonable. First off, there's only one single target boss, and second, I think most players would need to git gud before having their Flameshaper damage be higher and that's not even accounting for movement (less hover)
Marksmanship Hunter0.5%8%
Spoiler:
8% AoE, 4% M+ Overall

These buffs try to improve Marksmanship's very poor standing in Mythic+, but are simply not enough. Despite its primary AoE mechanic being hard-capped at 8 targets, it still does less 8-target AoE DPS than Beast Mastery which is uncapped, has endless DPS mobility, and is simpler to play. Marksmanship needs massive AoE and Priority buffs to even be remotely competitive. Hard-capped specs should not be defeated by uncapped specs within their target cap boundary.
Survival Hunter0%6.2%
Spoiler:
The hitbox of Wildfire Bomb is still detrimental
Fire Mage1%4-5%
Frost Mage1%5%
Spoiler:
Frost has continued to be outperformed by Arcane in most content, so these buffs to make it better in M+ are welcome. That said, this still doesn't do much to address the state of Frost's AoE rotation, in particular Blizzard still doesn't really have a role in the AoE rotation, which does not feel good.
Mistweaver Monk5.5%1%
Spoiler:
This tuning is definitely focused on direct, single-target healing. The 15% Vivify buff does not affect anything that comes additional from pressing Vivify - like Invigorating Mists and Zen Pulse, so this will only buff the direct portion.

Sheilun's Gift, on the other hand, has a natural AoE portion to it that does get increased by the 15% bonus to it, albeit most of its power does come from the main target heal. However, this does not account for too much of our healing done in Mythic+.

Single target healing is welcomed (and is honestly a major fault of Mistweaver Monk at the moment), but this is another round of increasingly small buffs to the spec while being at the very bottom of every chart in Raid (by a wide margin) and still doing pretty solidly in Mythic+ (due to most of the healing coming from damage-to-healing conversion, which is unaffected by healing tuning. Unfortunately, a 12.1.5 waiting room.
Windwalker Monk3-4%1-1.5%
Spoiler:
Windwalker gained 3-4% in single target in a much needed buff. This season has been rough for single target damage, especially compared to how strong Windwalker was in single target during Season 1. While this increase won’t entirely fix the problem, every little bit helps.

Windwalker’s strength in AoE likely makes it difficult to increase single target damage without pushing it from great to overpowered in Mythic+, which could be why Blizzard has taken a more gradual approach to single target buffs this season. However, where this buff falls short is that Rising Sun Kick continues to be quickly dropped when you have the Season 2 tier set buff and are playing  Conduit of the Celestials even in single target situations. This isn’t a game-breaking problem, but it is one that is counterintuitive to many of the new players who are coming to the spec this season. The buff to Rising Sun Kick damage does help, but since it doesn’t fix this specific problem, it will continue to be a point of confusion. The clear solution is to increase the buff that Rising Sun Kick gets from the tier set enough so that you still use it in single target and swap to more Spinning Crane Kick as more targets become available.

More single target damage is a welcome improvement for those that focus on raiding, and the Mythic+ enjoyers were already having a great time, so this fall into the category of being a good buff even if it doesn’t fix all the problems.
Protection Paladin6%6%
Retribution Paladin5%5%
Spoiler:
The listed values are for templar only. Herald has been the most popular Hero tree by a wide margin so far this season, partly due to the buffs it received in 12.0.7 and partly due to most of the encounters in the Venomous Abyss catering heavily to its sustained cleave niche. These buffs won't make Templar a stronger choice in that niche, but they should make it more competitive otherwise.
Discipline Priest0%17.5% (Oracle)
27% (VW)
Spoiler:
Voidweaver is recommended for best M+ hero spec now!
Shadow Priest5-7%0-1%
Spoiler:
This is a small buff aimed at giving shadow a little more boss and single target damage whilst trying to keep AoE and dungeon performance roughly the same. Shadow has been a strong choice for raid due to a large number of add and multi target fights, however, as those adds die faster and damage checks get more lenient the efficient spread cleave Shadow brings loses value. In dungeons, Shadow has had some issues with priority and boss damage, which this should help with, but it won't make the spec a meta contender.
Subtlety Rogue5% (Trickster)5% (Trickster)
Spoiler:
Trickster gets closer to Deathstalker but remains slightly behind in output. This is still a good change as Trickster is mechanically easier to play. Individuals who struggle with the rotation can test if their performance increases when switching hero talents.

This buff is only for the weaker hero talent, and it's not currently good.
Fury Warrior3%2%
Spoiler:
This is a passive boost to Mountain Thane, which will bring up its performance slightly with no change to the talents or rotation. Although it helps bridge the gap, Slayer is likely to remain preferred in most content, due to its better reliability.
Protection Warrior0%3.5%
Spoiler:
However, many top prot warriors are now opting for the Colossus tree in both ST and AoE, which this buff has no effect for.

summary.en: WoW: Forever Introduces New Weapon Effect to let Players Mine Without the Profession...
summary.es: WoW: Forever presenta un nuevo efecto de arma para permitir a los jugadores minar sin la profesión...

contentHtml:
In World of Warcraft: Forever, a familiar item in the Deadmines got an updated effect that allows players to mine without the mining profession!

Updated Rockslicer in WoW: Forever

Like gear across the game, loot from Deadmines received updated stats in WoW: Forever. One of the items, Rockslicer, now allows the wielder to mine Copper, Tin, Silver, and even Iron nodes for 30 charges. When all 30 charges are used, players will still have the weapon on them, but will lose its profession use.

Rockslicer
Item Level 23
Binds when picked up
Unique
Two-HandAxe
52 - 78 Damage Speed 3.30
(19.70 damage per second)
+10 Strength
Durability 65 / 65
Requires Level 18
Use: Slice open and gather from target Copper, Tin, Silver, or Iron Vein (does not require Mining).
30 Charges
Sell Price: 31 89

(note that the tooltip in game does not show the 30 charges to other players)


Without Rockslicer, a Miner would need a skill of 125 to mine Iron. Theoretically, a player could farm multiple Rockslicers and be able to mine Iron Deposit without the profession. This could be particularly attractive to players who picked both Engineering and Blacksmithing as their professions, especially early on, since they now have access to the ore without needing the Auction House (and could then have the ore smelted by a friend/guildie who is a miner).

Items like this open up a new path for players regarding trade skills, and could have a distinct impact on the economy as well. With the charges being limited, thankfully this isn't a required farm for most players, but it would be especially helpful to those who were already planning to farm for their materials for use or profit.

After you complete it and continue your questing, you'll notice a buff on your buff bar called Campfire Nearby. When you notice this, you can scan the area for a campsite, sit down at it, and get the buffs. You don't need to be in a party with the person who placed the campsite or any of the buffs; simply walk over and type "/sit" and hang out for a minute.

title.es: El acogedor saco de dormir está de vuelta en WoW: Forever

summary.en: Cozy Sleeping Bag is Back in WoW: Forever...
summary.es: Cozy Sleeping Bag está de vuelta en WoW: Forever...

contentHtml:
Players have been delighted to discover that the Cozy Sleeping Bag Quest Chain (originally from Season of Discovery) is now available in Forever.

Thank you to Brubby from The WoW Secret Finding Discord for confirming this and providing screenshots. If you think Secret Finding is for you, you can join the Discord at the link below:


Wow Secret Finding Discord


The Cozy Sleeping Bag is an item (with a 1-hour cooldown) that enables you to get cozy anywhere. You can put down your Sleeping Bag and have a quick lie-down to gain a 1% experience buff every minute, up to a maximum of 3% buff. You'll need to take a nap after all the running you need to do to get it!





While 3% experience may not sound like much on its own, if you combine this with other buffs (such as the 5% experience buff available from cooking), it can quickly add up.

As a reward for time spent on the trail, you will also receive 5x Student Fodder (which in Season of Discovery gave 20% of a level of rested experience) and a 12-slot bag from Stepping Stones.


Cozy Sleeping Bag Guide


Our guide walks you through all the steps to claim your own Cozy Sleeping Bag, but if you would rather explore for yourself, you can find the starting points for both Horde and Alliance below. Be warned, though: it has been reported that, at present, the quests are visibly marked in-game. We are unsure if this is intended, and so if you would rather complete this blind, you may prefer to hold off until launch.

Where to start the Cozy Sleeping Bag Quest Chain in WoW: Forever

If you are level 14 or above, you can complete this quest now on the beta. The start points for both Horde and Alliance are below:

title.en: New Cosmetic-Only Reward Discovered in WoW: Forever
title.es: Nueva recompensa solo para cosméticos descubierta en WoW: Forever

summary.en: New Cosmetic-Only Reward Discovered in WoW: Forever...
summary.es: Nueva recompensa solo para cosméticos descubierta en WoW: para siempre...

contentHtml:
Players have discovered a cosmetic-only item in WoW: Forever, similar to how Retail handles cosmetic appearances.

WoW: Forever will include an opt-in transmog system for those who want to use it. Players who want to see transmogs on themselves and others can opt in, while players who want to see the exact models of gear that players have equipped can keep the setting toggled off.

Now that the WoW: Forever beta is live, "Gloky" has submitted a screenshot to Wowhead of a transmog-only item on the Gadgetzan reputation vendor. Stolen Wastewander Cowl is sold at Revered reputation for 10.

  


This cosmetic-only item is new to Forever with the transmog system, but players who have experienced Retail will be familiar with the concept. If you're playing with Transmog off, then there's no need to buy this other than for collections. It's currently unknown if there are other items similar to this, or if this is an oversight that might be changed before official launch.

title.en: [Retracted] Experience Values in WoW Forever Same as Classic
title.es: [Retracted] Los valores de la experiencia en WoW Forever son los mismos que en Classic

summary.en: [Retracted] Experience Values in WoW Forever Same as Classic...
summary.es: [Retracted] Los valores de experiencia en WoW para siempre son los mismos que los clásicos...

contentHtml:
More Information:
Blainie: After reviewing the values in the table, as well as Blizzard reaching out regarding this article, we can confirm that there are no changes to the experience amounts required to level in WoW Forever. The values that were found via datamining were in a file that isn't actually used by the game version it comes from, with a different file that wasn't visible to us initially being used instead.

Blizzard clarified how the experience values are pulled for that specific version of WoW and the values match WoW Forever.

This isn't something we take lightly, nor is it the fault of any individual at Wowhead - there are processes in place to move from finding a data point to actually writing the news, and while there are review processes in place, the data we had in front of us was, well, "correct" based on the files we were looking at. Clearly, it wasn't correct.

The rate at which people level in Forever is a widely discussed topic, with changes to dungeon experience, new quests making zones "last longer", etc. - I'll be the first to admit that we thought we had found something that was big news for the community. We should have verified again that what we were seeing was in fact true - we didn't and that's my fault, as the head of the team that contributed to this minformation going out.

We made a pretty massive mistake with this post and will most certainly be checking things a lot more rigorously before posting in the future. We can't take back that this post went out, nor that it will cause discussions in the future of "Wowhead said" - we also know it will take time to regain trust in the accuracy of the articles we put out.

I can't fix that it went out. I will be leaving the post up simply as an example of our failings, with this disclaimer - I will not delete it to "hide" it.

I can only apologise that it happened and can assure you it will not happen again.

P.S. I've already seen some of the posts coming in to the writer of this article, as well as others on the team. I understand that many of you are angry - if you are, and you want to talk about this post, or Wowhead, the state of it, or the problems you've identified in this procedure, my DMs are open. You can reach me on Discord at "blainiewow" or via the Wowhead Discord. Please don't continue witch-hunting members of the Wowhead team.
Forever changes many things about Classic, including the EXP curve required to level up! EXP requirements are a hot-button topic for a lot of Classic players, and while Blizzard has tuned experience gains from Dungeon Quests, the actual amount of experience needed to level has also changed significantly according to our datamining.

Smooth and Gradual

Era and SoD servers had a very specific leveling path that players were very familiar with. Now, though, it looks like Forever is making changes to adjust that curve. The main takeaway from the data is that the new experience curve is a gradual climb up to 60, rather than a series of spikes.

In Classic, there were two spikes in experience required: going from level 39 to 40, and from 59 to 60. These levels match up with learning mounts and hitting max level, and traditionally had much higher experience requirements than similar levels. We've previously noted that the profile of dungeon experience was changing (from mob-heavy to quest-heavy), and these experience changes dovetail with an overall reduction in the amount of experience needed to reach level 60.

In Forever, the spikes in required experience no longer exist; instead, it follows a gradual quadratic climb per level. Overall experience has also dropped significantly, with the biggest reductions between levels 15 and 30, where the total reduction averages over 40%. This reduction eases in higher levels, but the 30 to 45 level bracket still sees a reduction of over 30%. Overall, experience required from 1 to 60 has dropped by a staggering 26%. Levels 1 through 5 are unchanged.

The Future of Leveling

Leveling in Forever and other versions of Classic is a big part of the game, and these changes significantly speed up many areas that have been both iconic and painful. Players might remember quests around level 35 not being very centralized anymore and requiring a lot of running around, or levels 50-60 being a long stretch to the end of their journey. These changes ease those pain points significantly and directly incentivize replayability.

By leveling faster, players simply won't have the time to explore and quest through as many zones as one might expect. Those zones, however, could be played through on a second or third character. For players looking to speed through the leveling process, the combined change to experience requirements and dungeon quests should also make leveling significantly smoother.

That said, given that players will be capped at level 60 forever in Forever, some players may be concerned that the leveling process is too fast. Many players have noticed that leaving a starting zone now gets them close to level 12 in many situations, whereas before, in SoD or Era realms, a character would be slightly underleveled heading into the next zone. While the beta only allows players to level to 20, it's also a possibility that experience is tuned higher to allow greater accessibility during testing in a limited timeframe.
